Contact Center AI Routing·Value hypothesis
Slide 3 / 7
Section 2 · Value hypothesis

The case rests on one falsifiable claim — AI routing lifts containment from 28% to the stated 40% target; if a pilot does not move it, the case is wrong.

A value hypothesis earns its place only if it can be proven false. This one is anchored on a recorded baseline and a stated KPI target — a pilot is the test.

Falsifiable value claim
AI-assisted routing lifts Contact Center Containment from the recorded 28% baseline toward the 40% target stated in the KPI dictionary, while holding or improving CSAT — without replacing agents.
Baseline28 percent
→
MechanismSkill-aware routing places each contact with the right-skilled agent or self-service path first time — lifting containment, cutting repeat transfers (18.4% today), and reducing the mix-shift pressure on AHT.
→
Target40 percent (stated KPI target)
Falsification testA Customer Care pilot that does not move containment by ~4 points on piloted queues falsifies the hypothesis — the Charter is then reshaped or stopped, not advanced to build.
So whatA pilot on Customer Care queues is the falsification test; the hypothesis is provable, not asserted.
Decision roleConfirm the value claim is falsifiable and tied to a recorded baseline metric.
OwnerPriya Iyer (Program Lead)
Evidence2 sources · as of 2026-04-30 · confidence Medium · 2 open gaps
Next gateDesign & Plan pilot scope — the falsification test
